page: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 32 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU runs at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled as a local 1890 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core and multi-core performance. The processor achieves top-25% scores in stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations. It demonstrates top-tier performance in text generation for small language models at 344.97 tokens per second, alongside strong prompt processing capabilities. Cryptographic operations are highly efficient, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instruction sets, placing its Passmark CPU encryption test in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth and database operations fall within the average range, with uncached read speeds at 80.53 GB/sec and write speeds at 58.7 GB/sec.

The D32alds_v6 provides a cost-efficient profile for compute-intensive workloads that do not demand large memory footprints. By constraining memory to 2.0 GB per vCPU, users avoid paying for unutilized RAM while leveraging high-frequency AMD EPYC processing power and fast local NVMe storage. However, the 64 GB memory limit represents a tradeoff for memory-bound applications or massive databases. This configuration is highly suited for compute-heavy tasks, software compilation, image and text processing, web serving, and small-scale LLM inference.
